limitations: No implementation was made because the workspace is read-only and the task requested security context only.

The target repository contains no observed ApoMarioHighscore, highscore panel, or recordRunEnd symbols; proposed enforcement points therefore use the existing final-score, panel initialization, analysis display, and donor highscore symbols.
The exact Path source, persistence format, bounds, time unit, and eligibility of replay/AI/simulation/editor runs remain unresolved.

nodes.label: Persisted highscore records: player name, score, survival time
Finished run result and its actual score
Highscore menu presentation and score ordering
Local highscore store boundary
nodes.sink: ApoMarioHighscore in-memory names, scores, survival times and the file write used for persistence.
nodes.source: ApoMarioHighscore(Path) loading and persistAcrossRuns/storeRun operations; donor load parses integer and name fields from an external stream.
nodes.untrusted_input: The file selected by the Path passed to the highscore store, including records a local user can edit or truncate.

nodes.label: Level-content decoding boundary
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevel allocation and construction, which later supplies width, time, players and finish state to score calculation.
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevelIO#readLevel(DataInputStream) and ApoMarioEditorIO#readLevel(DataInputStream) read attacker-editable integers and booleans.
nodes.untrusted_input: Binary level content from a local file or shared level source, including dimensions, timers, tile values, enemy counts and coordinates.

nodes.label: Finished-run integration boundary
nodes.sink: The proposed ApoMarioHighscore#storeRun call and its persisted highscore record.
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean) computes and mutates player points; ApoMarioPlayer exposes points and team-name accessors; ApoMarioLevel exposes remaining and passed time.
nodes.untrusted_input: In-game values that a local user can tamper with to cheat, including player points, player/team name, replay state and remaining timer.

nodes.label: ApoMario calculates final score adjustments, calls component.setBWin, and then transitions to the analysis view; the one-player winning path adds finish and time/difficulty/width points to playerOne before setAnalysis returns.
nodes.task_relevance: This is the primary integration point for recording the finished run after actual score mutation and before the result is displayed.
nodes.verification: Exercise both bWin=true and bWin=false paths and verify the stored score equals the post-adjustment player score shown by ApoMarioAnalysis.

nodes.label: ApoMarioAnalysis displays points on both the win and game-over result paths; its getName method uses replay names, human, or AI team names.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore panel should reuse the same player-name semantics while avoiding recording replay/simulation results unless explicitly intended by the implementation.
nodes.verification: Run a human game, AI game, replay, win and loss; compare the recorded name and score with the analysis result.

nodes.label: ApoIcarus keeps parallel names, time and points lists, loads triples from an external stream, and its highscore view inserts records before lower-point records to produce descending score order.
nodes.task_relevance: These are the donor implementation patterns to adapt for the required Path-backed ApoMarioHighscore API and dedicated panel.
nodes.verification: Seed a store with unsorted records, reload it, and assert names, scores and times remain index-aligned and scores are descending.

nodes.failure_behavior: Observed code returns false only for malformed URL or I/O errors; malformed numeric records are not explicitly rejected and reported at the parser boundary.
nodes.label: The donor load operation accepts external lines and calls Integer.valueOf without validating range, record completeness, or list alignment; malformed numeric content can escape the IOException handlers, and partial triples can produce inconsistent parallel lists.
nodes.task_relevance: Reusing this implementation directly for a local editable store could make highscore loading fail unpredictably or corrupt displayed associations.
nodes.verification: Supply malformed, incomplete and oversized records and confirm the adapted parser rejects each input without changing the prior valid in-memory board.

nodes.failure_behavior: Observed decoder does not show bounds checks before allocation or loop execution; malformed input may throw or consume excessive resources.
nodes.label: Level decoders allocate arrays from untrusted width and height and iterate attacker-controlled counts and coordinates before any visible validation; a malformed shared or local level can cause excessive allocation, long processing, or invalid game state.
nodes.task_relevance: The new highscore flow reads level-derived time and score, so malformed level content can affect the values sent to storage.
nodes.verification: Use truncated, negative, maximal and inconsistent dimensions/counts and verify decoding rejects them before allocation or unbounded iteration.

nodes.failure_behavior: Proposed adapted operation rejects invalid score, time, name length/content and store-path conditions, reports the rejection, and does not substitute or clamp values.
nodes.label: A public storeRun operation that accepts score, survival time and playerName can be called with forged values or hostile names, allowing tampered rankings, misleading identity, malformed persistence, or resource abuse.
nodes.task_relevance: The required public API is directly exposed to local callers and tests; validation must be inside the receiving store operation.
nodes.verification: Call storeRun with null, blank, oversized and control-character names, negative and extreme integers, and an unusable Path; assert false or the specified rejection result, a diagnostic, and no new record.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report invalid records; leave the existing board unchanged. Do not clamp or replace the caller's values at this parser/store boundary.
nodes.label: ApoMarioHighscore#storeRun must validate the complete record before insertion or persistence: require a bounded nonblank playerName, a nonnegative bounded score, and a nonnegative bounded survivalTime, preserve the three fields as one aligned record, sort records by score descending, and report rejection without substituting or clamping invalid input.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects highscore integrity and the required names/scores/survival-times API at its first receiving operation.
nodes.verification: Unit-test valid records, equal scores, invalid fields, duplicate records and ordering; verify all three getters have equal length and matching indices.

nodes.failure_behavior: At the integration point, normalize missing name/time to stated safe defaults and continue recording; do not skip the run. The receiving store still rejects invalid input and reports it.
nodes.label: The finished-run integration must call recordRunEnd(level) exactly once after ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis has finalized the actual player's score, and must pass the actual player name and elapsed survival time in seconds or milliseconds converted consistently to the required mm:ss display value; on missing or invalid integration values, use documented defaults before calling storeRun so the primary recording effect still occurs.
nodes.task_relevance: Ensures wins and losses are recorded from the running game rather than from display-only or stale values.
nodes.verification: Instrument recordRunEnd and complete a win, timeout loss and player death; assert one call per run, post-finalization score, expected name, and nonnegative elapsed time.

nodes.failure_behavior: If persisted content is invalid, show an empty or last-known-valid board and report the rejection; still allow the menu and panel to open. If the panel action is unavailable, preserve normal menu operation.
nodes.label: The dedicated ApoMario highscore panel must load validated persisted records, expose names, scores and survival times in aligned descending-score order, render player name and mm:ss time, and be reachable from the menu with persistence initialized across runs.
nodes.task_relevance: Covers the requested menu integration, display and persistence behavior using the donor panel pattern.
nodes.verification: Start the game twice using the same store, open the menu highscore action, and verify records survive restart, display names and mm:ss values, and remain score-descending.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return false or the API's documented rejection result and report the reason; never insert a rejected record, never clamp it, and never discard already-valid records.
nodes.label: Implement the adapted Path-backed store operation with bounded text/numeric checks, a single record representation or transactionally aligned fields, descending-score insertion, and explicit rejection reporting; write only validated records and retain the previous valid board when persistence fails.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R1 while preserving the effect of valid runs and preventing malformed local data from changing rankings.
nodes.verification: Fault-inject invalid records and file-write failures; verify rejection is observable, valid prior data remains readable, and a subsequent valid storeRun still succeeds.

nodes.failure_behavior: If level-derived values are missing or invalid, substitute the stated defaults at this integration point and call the store; if the store rejects the normalized record, report the rejection without suppressing the run completion or menu transition.
nodes.label: Place the recording call in the finalized setAnalysis path after score mutations and before the analysis transition, select the human/AI/replay name according to the intended run policy, derive elapsed time from the level timer, and normalize missing name to "human" and invalid elapsed time to zero before invoking storeRun.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R2 at the change's primary integration point while ensuring a valid run still produces a highscore record.
nodes.verification: Test null AI/team name, negative/expired timer, replay, editor and simulation modes; verify the chosen policy and defaulting behavior are deterministic and recording remains attempted.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report invalid persisted records, use an empty/last-known-valid board for display, and keep menu navigation operational; do not let a malformed store disable the game.
nodes.label: Initialize one ApoMarioHighscore instance with a defined application-local Path during panel initialization, add a menu action and dedicated panel state modeled on ApoJumpStateHighscore, and render only validated records using fixed-width mm:ss formatting; isolate load failures so the menu remains usable.
nodes.task_relevance: Enforces R3 while preserving availability when the editable store is damaged.
nodes.verification: Corrupt, truncate and enlarge the store, then launch and navigate the game; verify rejection is reported, no unbounded allocation occurs, and the highscore panel remains usable.

nodes.label: The inspected sources do not establish the intended persistent file location, record format, maximum number of entries, maximum name length, exact survival-time unit, or whether replay, AI, editor and simulation runs should enter the public board.
nodes.task_relevance: These choices affect validation bounds, compatibility, ordering, and whether recordRunEnd can distinguish eligible runs; implementation and tests need an explicit policy.
nodes.verification: Define these policies in the implementation and test fixtures before relying on persistence or recordRunEnd behavior.

summary: ApoMario currently computes final player points in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis, exposes player names and scores through ApoMarioPlayer, and displays run results in ApoMarioAnalysis, but has no observed highscore panel or local highscore store. ApoIcarus provides reusable highscore storage and descending-score panel logic; its network parser is not suitable unchanged for the fixed desktop/local-file threat model.
